lines_of_business: Medicare Advantage: LCD L33618 Major Joint Replacement (Hip and Knee) reviewed
sections_in_order: Position Statement (Total hip arthroplasty, Revision arthroplasty, Hip resurfacing)
criteria_location: Position Statement pp.1-3: THA and revision (p.1-2), contraindication footnote, resurfacing (p.2-3).

logic.top_level: pathways (THA, revision, total resurfacing, partial resurfacing); THA is any-of-7 conditions where the last one carries ALL sub-criteria

k_of_n.quote: meets the definition of medical necessity when 1 or more of the following conditions exist

logic.exclusions_or_contraindications: Starred contraindication lists: THA/revision (active systemic bacteremia; active skin infection or open wound; neuropathic arthritis; rapidly progressive neurological disease) and resurfacing (10 items incl. female of childbearing age).
logic.initial_vs_repeat: Revision pathway separate; no repeat-procedure rules.

and_or_ambiguity.quote: Advanced joint disease demonstrated by ... (subchondral cysts, ... avascular necrosis), AND o Pain or functional disability ..., AND o Failure of at least 3 months of conservative ... No contraindications* to total hip arthroplasty for any indication above are present
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: The AND items follow only the last OR item (advanced joint disease) by indentation, but the contraindication line is dedented and reads as applying to all seven indications.

and_or_ambiguity.quote: Partial hip resurfacing ... Has known or suspected metal sensitivity or concern about potential effects of metal ions There is no more than 50% involvement
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: Metal sensitivity is a contraindication for total resurfacing but required for partial; bullet lacks AND; reads as odd/conflicting.
undefined; history says criteria revised 'for clarity' but no detail

requirement_kinds.quote: Malignancy ...; Avascular necrosis; Fracture of the femoral neck; Acetabular fracture; Failure of previous hip surgery; Mal-union of acetabular or proximal femur fracture
Advanced joint disease demonstrated by radiographic or MRI evidence of subchondral cysts, subchondral sclerosis, periarticular osteophytes, joint subluxation, joint space narrowing
Pain or functional disability from injury due to trauma or arthritis of the joint

Failure of at least 3 months of conservative non-surgical management ... includes 1 or more of the following: anti-inflammatory, analgesics, exercises, supervised PT, activity restrictions, assistive device, weight reduction
Likely to outlive a traditional prosthesis (eg, age 55 or younger)
no more than 50% involvement of the femoral head; minimal change in acetabular cartilage
Severely overweight (without attempted weight loss or discussion of increased risk related to BMI) is a contraindication to resurfacing

time_windows.quote: at least 3 months of conservative non-surgical management
